asset: texture import (lossy WebP, uncompressed in VRAM)
notes: Model textures decode to RGBA8 in video memory (1.0-1.9 GB); VRAM compression would cut it ~4x but grows the download: a decision.

The moor's oak (hundreds on screen across Act I). Its own canopy is crumpled shards in a model sheet, but in play the game's leaf clusters cover it and it reads as a full, rooted oak. A procedural Blender replacement (tools/blender/trees/oak_gen.py: bark baked from a procedural material, one UV island per branch) was built and compared in the game (oak_compare.gd) and rejected: sparse, oversized, bare limbs. Better fix: Meshy with a modelled canopy.
Autumn oak: same; full in play.
